bark_morrow_4.ja: 「君は彼に、それを諦めろと言うのか？」

e_rival_adrian.ja: レーベルのスターリング

ei_rival_adrian.en: The executive at the head of the glass table slides the contract an inch toward you instead. "You're the 'she' in the song. Then you can tell him what's good for the song."
ei_rival_adrian.ja: ガラスのテーブルの上座の重役が、契約書をあなたのほうへ少し滑らせる。「君が歌の中の『彼女』か。なら、何が歌のためになるか彼に言えるだろう」

ew_rival_adrian.en: Sterling caps his pen. "Keep your line, then," he says. "Nobody will hear it." He doesn't look like he believes that either.
ew_rival_adrian.ja: スターリングはペンにキャップをする。「その一行は取っておけばいい。誰も聞かないさ」彼自身もそうは思っていない顔だ。

pre_sterling.en: The executive at the head of the glass table slides the contract an inch toward you instead. "You're the 'she' in the song. Then you can tell him what's good for the song."
pre_sterling.ja: ガラスのテーブルの上座の重役が、契約書をあなたのほうへ少し滑らせる。「君が歌の中の『彼女』か。なら、何が歌のためになるか彼に言えるだろう」

post_sterling.en: Sterling caps his pen. "Keep your line, then," he says. "Nobody will hear it." He doesn't look like he believes that either.
post_sterling.ja: スターリングはペンにキャップをする。「その一行は取っておけばいい。誰も聞かないさ」彼自身もそうは思っていない顔だ。

bark_sterling_1.ja: 「ヒットには理由がある。修正だ」

bark_sterling_2.en: He turns the pen in his fingers.

bark_sterling_3.ja: 「感傷は売れない。コラボは売れる」

bark_sterling_4.ja: 「君の一行で、何百万を捨てるのか？」

ei_rival_fushen.en: At the head of the long table the patriarch sets down his chopsticks. The room goes quiet with him. "Someone he brought in from outside," he says, to nobody, about you.
ei_rival_fushen.ja: 長いテーブルの上座で、当主が箸を置く。部屋が彼と一緒に静まる。「外から連れてきた者か」誰にともなく、あなたについてそう言う。

ew_rival_fushen.en: The old man looks at you for a long moment, then at his grandson's hand on the table beside yours. He picks his chopsticks back up. Nobody mentions the other family again.
ew_rival_fushen.ja: 老人は長いあいだあなたを見つめ、それから、あなたの手の隣にある孫の手を見る。彼は再び箸を取る。もう誰も、あの家の話をしない。

pre_fu_elder.en: At the head of the long table the patriarch sets down his chopsticks. The room goes quiet with him. "Someone he brought in from outside," he says, to nobody, about you.
pre_fu_elder.ja: 長いテーブルの上座で、当主が箸を置く。部屋が彼と一緒に静まる。「外から連れてきた者か」誰にともなく、あなたについてそう言う。

post_fu_elder.en: The old man looks at you for a long moment, then at his grandson's hand on the table beside yours. He picks his chopsticks back up. Nobody mentions the other family again.
post_fu_elder.ja: 老人は長いあいだあなたを見つめ、それから、あなたの手の隣にある孫の手を見る。彼は再び箸を取る。もう誰も、あの家の話をしない。

bark_fu_elder_1.en: "This house has a hundred years of rules."
bark_fu_elder_1.ja: 「この家には百年の決まりがある」

bark_fu_elder_2.en: He folds both hands over the head of his cane.
bark_fu_elder_2.ja: 彼は杖の柄に両手を重ねる。

t_subtitle.en: An otome dating sim RPG. Six men, one evening star — plan the date, win him over.
t_subtitle.ja: 乙女恋愛シミュレーションRPG。六人の男、ひとつの宵の明星 — デートを計画し、彼の心をほどく。

t_note.en: 18+ · Otome · All characters are adults · AI-generated work (see 'About this work')
t_note.ja: 18歳以上対象 · 乙女向け · 登場人物は全員成人です · AI生成作品（「作品について」参照）

ds_adult.en: This game is for adults (18+). Every character is an adult and is stated as one; every intimate scene is consensual and asked for on the page. Contains sexual content (no explicit genitals).
ds_adult.ja: 本作品は成人向け（18歳以上）です。登場人物はすべて成人で、作中でもそう明記されています。親密な場面はすべて合意のうえで、その意思が作中で確かめられます。性的な表現を含みます（性器の描写はありません）。

about_ai.en: AI disclosure: Generative AI is used as a production tool in this work, which was made through intensive collaboration between the developer and AI over several hundred hours. Images (sprites, backgrounds, CGs) are output by an image-generation model and the voice by a speech-synthesis model. The concept, world, story structure, direction, character design, the selection and compositing of every image, voice direction, game-system design and balancing, and testing are the developer's work; the script text and the program were written and edited jointly by AI language models and the developer.
about_ai.ja: 【AI使用について】本作は生成AIを制作ツールとして活用し、開発者とAIの集中的な共同作業で制作しました。画像（立ち絵・背景・CG）は画像生成AIで出力し、音声は音声合成AIで生成しています。企画・世界観・ストーリー構成・演出・キャラクター設計、すべての画像の選定と合成、音声の演技指示、ゲームシステムの設計とバランス調整、テストは開発者が行い、シナリオ文とプログラムはAI（大規模言語モデル）と開発者が共同で執筆・編集しています。制作には数百時間を費やしています。

lang_note.en: All seven languages cover the interface, the RPG text, every standoff and the six routes' story; voice is in English.
lang_note.ja: 七言語すべてで、インターフェース、RPG部分の文章、すべての対峙、六つのルートの本編を収録しています。ボイスは英語です。

toast_trust.en: Trust %d — he has let you a little further in
toast_trust.ja: 信頼 %d — 彼はあなたを少し内側へ入れた

lose_standoff.en: The distance won: the moment closed. Nothing is lost but the last few minutes — you are back at the last save, just before it.
lose_standoff.ja: 距離が勝ち、その瞬間は閉じてしまった。失ったのは数分だけ — 直前のセーブに戻る。

lose_dawn.en: The last train goes without you and the night closes without him. You are back at the last save.
lose_dawn.ja: 終電はあなたを置いて出て、夜は彼のいないまま閉じた。最後のセーブに戻る。

t_trial.ja: 体験版 — 顧言 第1〜2章

fin_body.en: Level %d · Trust %d. Thank you for playing. Your last save is in slot 1. Five more men are waiting at the title: every route has three endings.
fin_body.ja: レベル %d · 信頼 %d。プレイしていただきありがとうございました。最後のセーブはスロット1に。タイトルではあと五人が待っています — どのルートにも三つのエンディングがあります。

nc_budget.en: %d turns until the last train. Moving, searching and standoffs all cost time.
nc_budget.ja: 終電まで %d 手。移動・調べる・対峙はすべて時間を使う。

h_clock.en: %s   ·   %d turns to the last train   ·   Lv %d

b_weak_hit.en: It lands — that is one of his tells.
b_weak_hit.ja: 届いた — それは彼の弱いところ。

b_resist_hit.en: It slides off. He sees it coming.
b_resist_hit.ja: かわされた。見抜かれている。

b_threat_mark.en: You pushed. He will remember it: the distance grows faster for the rest of this.
b_threat_mark.ja: 押しすぎた。彼は忘れない：この先、距離は速く広がる。

b_enemy_turn.ja: %s は身を引く。距離 %+d。%s の平静 −%d。

b_lose.en: It is over. He has closed the door.
b_lose.ja: 終わった。彼は扉を閉じた。

r_needs_keepsake.en: Needs a keepsake — something to remember together.

r_needs_treat.en: Needs something sweet from the café.
r_needs_treat.ja: カフェの甘いものが必要。

tr_end_title.en: This is where the trial ends.

tr_end_body.en: Gu Yan's chapters 3–5 and all three of his endings, five more men with five chapters and three endings each, every date and rival standoff, all 18 CGs and growth to level 20 are in the full version. Your trial save carries over.
tr_end_body.ja: 顧言の第3〜5章と三つのエンディング、それぞれ五章・三エンディングを持つほか五人のルート、すべてのデートとライバルとの対峙、全18枚のCG、レベル20までの成長は製品版に収録されています。体験版のセーブデータは製品版に引き継げます。

tr_open_store.ja: 製品版のページを開く

sd_wit.en: Banter, remembering, saying it plainly; your nerve pool.
sd_wit.ja: 軽口・思い出す・率直に言う。胆力の上限。

sd_cha.en: Teasing, something sweet, a look that lingers.
sd_cha.ja: からかう・甘いもの・見つめる。

sd_grt.en: Composure; how much the distance can cost you.
sd_grt.ja: 平静の上限。距離に耐える力。

sd_stl.en: Breathing brings the distance down further.
sd_stl.ja: 「深呼吸」で距離を大きく縮める。

ad_deflect.en: Give him room: soften his next move and close the distance a little.
ad_deflect.ja: 彼に余白を：次の一手を和らげ、距離を少し縮める。

ad_observe.en: Watch him: reveals his tells (what reaches him).
ad_observe.ja: 彼を見る：弱いところ（彼に届くもの）が分かる。

ad_banter.ja: 軽やかに切り返す。機知。

ad_tease.en: Warmth with a smile in it. Charm.
ad_tease.ja: 笑みを含んだ温かさ。魅力。

ad_remember.en: Bring up something only the two of you know. Closes the distance. Needs a keepsake.
ad_remember.ja: 二人だけが知っていることを持ち出す。距離が縮む。思い出の品が必要。

ad_sweet.en: Share something from the café. Charm. Needs a treat.
ad_sweet.ja: カフェの甘いものを分ける。魅力。お菓子が必要。

ad_push.en: Ask for more than he is offering. Hits hard — and he remembers: the distance grows faster for the rest of the date.
ad_push.ja: 彼が差し出す以上を求める。強く響くが、彼は忘れない：この先、距離は速く広がる。

ad_stall.en: Slow down and let the quiet work. The distance falls; a little composure back.
ad_stall.ja: ゆっくりと、沈黙に任せる。距離が縮み、平静が少し戻る。

ad_item.ja: バッグの中のものを使う。

ad_plain.en: Say the true thing, without decoration. Closes the distance.
ad_plain.ja: 飾らずに本当のことを言う。距離が縮む。

ad_linger.en: Hold his eyes a beat longer than you should. Closes the distance.
ad_linger.ja: 少しだけ長く、彼の目を見つめる。距離が縮む。

skd_glow.ja: からかう +40%、長いまなざし +30%。

id_macarons.en: A box from the café. For 'Something sweet'.
id_macarons.ja: カフェの箱入り。「甘いもの」に使う。

id_transit.en: Gets you across the city after dark.
id_transit.ja: 夜の街を渡るための定期。

id_trench.en: For rain and long walks. Poise +1, Patience +1, Breathe +20%.
id_trench.ja: 雨と長い散歩に。落ち着き +1、辛抱 +1、深呼吸 +20%。

i_slip.ja: ワインレッドのスリップドレス

id_slip.en: Charm +3, Tease +30%, A look that lingers +20%.
id_slip.ja: 魅力 +3、からかう +30%、長いまなざし +20%。

id_his_shirt.en: Too big, and yours now. Charm +2, Poise +2, A look that lingers +30%, Say it plainly +20%.
id_his_shirt.ja: 大きすぎて、もうあなたのもの。魅力 +2、落ち着き +2、長いまなざし +30%、率直に言う +20%。

id_perfume.en: Charm +1, Tease +20%, A look that lingers +20%.
id_perfume.ja: 魅力 +1、からかう +20%、長いまなざし +20%。

id_notebook.en: You write down what he says. Wit +1, Remember +30%.
id_notebook.ja: 彼の言葉を書き留める。機知 +1、思い出す +30%。

pl_day_1.en: Monday. You have the evening, and a plan to make.
pl_day_1.ja: 月曜日。夜は空いている。計画を立てよう。

pl_day_2.en: Tuesday. You already know a little more about him than last time.
pl_day_2.ja: 火曜日。前より少しだけ、彼のことを知っている。

pl_day_3.en: Wednesday. Halfway through the week, and he is on your mind more than halfway.
pl_day_3.ja: 水曜日。週の半ば。彼のことは半分以上、頭にある。

pl_day_4.en: Thursday. Something is pressing on him; plan for that.
pl_day_4.ja: 木曜日。何かが彼にのしかかっている。それを踏まえて計画を。

pl_day_5.en: Friday. The last evening of the week. Make it the right one.
pl_day_5.ja: 金曜日。週の最後の夜。正しい夜にしよう。

pl_hint_guyan.en: Gu Yan closes the shop at nine and likes the quiet hour after. Something warm before you go; no rush; dress for rain.
pl_hint_guyan.ja: 顧言は九時に店を閉め、その後の静かな時間が好き。行く前に温かいものを。急がずに。雨に備えた装いで。

pl_hint_ethan.en: Ethan works until the building empties. He respects people who don't waste his time: go straight to him, say what you mean, and dress like you work on the top floor.
pl_hint_ethan.ja: イーサンはビルが空になるまで働く。時間を無駄にしない人を尊重する：まっすぐ彼のもとへ、思ったことを言い、最上階で働く人のような装いで。

pl_hint_luxingye.en: Lu Xingye can't be seen in public as himself. Take the long way through the city, keep it light and teasing, and wear something that feels like a night out.
pl_hint_luxingye.ja: 陸星野は素顔で人前に出られない。遠回りして街を歩き、軽やかにからかって、夜遊びらしい装いで。

pl_hint_liam.en: Liam is off shift at seven and hates fuss. A walk first, a joke or two, and what you'd wear to a neighbour's porch.
pl_hint_liam.ja: リアムは七時に非番になり、大げさなことが苦手。まず散歩、冗談をひとつふたつ、そしてお隣のポーチに行くような服で。

pl_hint_adrian.en: Adrian is bored of people who perform. Go straight to him, mean every word, and wear something with an edge.
pl_hint_adrian.ja: エイドリアンは演じる人に飽きている。まっすぐ彼のもとへ、言葉はすべて本気で、少し尖った装いで。

pl_hint_fushen.en: Fu Shen notices everything and says nothing. Somewhere quiet first, take your time, and dress like the room you're walking into.
pl_hint_fushen.ja: 傅深はすべてに気づき、何も言わない。まず静かな場所へ、時間をかけて、向かう部屋にふさわしい装いで。

pl_q_way.en: How do you want to be with him tonight?
pl_q_way.ja: 今夜、彼とどう過ごしたい？

pl_fit.ja: それは彼に合っている。

pl_miss.en: Not quite him — but it's your evening too.
pl_miss.ja: 彼らしくはない — でも、あなたの夜でもある。

pl_wear_ok.en: And what you're wearing is exactly his kind of evening.
pl_wear_ok.ja: そしてその装いは、まさに彼好みの夜だ。

pl_wear_no.en: You catch yourself in the mirror: lovely — but not quite his evening. (Change in the Party menu; the wardrobe is here.)
pl_wear_no.ja: 鏡に映る自分：素敵だけど、彼の好みとは少し違う。（着替えは「パーティ」メニューから。クローゼットはここ）

pl_good.en: The plan fits him (2 of 3 or better): Trust +1, and his guard starts lower tonight.
pl_good.ja: 計画は彼にぴったり（3つ中2つ以上）：信頼 +1、今夜は心の壁が低いところから始まる。

pl_bad.en: The plan doesn't quite fit him (fewer than 2 of 3): the date starts at his full guard.
pl_bad.ja: 計画は彼に合わなかった（3つ中2つ未満）：デートは心の壁が高いまま始まる。

ev_wardrobe.en: You open the wardrobe and stand there longer than you need to, deciding who you are going to be tonight.
ev_wardrobe.ja: クローゼットを開け、必要以上に長く立ち尽くす。今夜の自分を決めるために。

ev_wardrobe_n.en: Nothing new in here — but the mirror says you look like someone who is expected somewhere.
ev_wardrobe_n.ja: 新しいものはない — でも鏡の中のあなたは、どこかで待たれている人の顔をしている。

ev_desk.en: Your desk, the half-finished things on it, and the one thing you came back for.
ev_desk.ja: 机の上の、やりかけのものたち。そして取りに戻ったひとつ。

ev_counter.en: The barista knows your order by now, and adds something you didn't ask for. "You've got a look," she says. "Go on."
ev_counter.ja: バリスタはもうあなたの注文を覚えていて、頼んでいないものをひとつ添える。「いい顔してる。行っておいで」

ev_corner.en: You sit by the window for a minute and let the evening rearrange itself. Something in your bag has his name on it now.
ev_corner.ja: 窓際に一分だけ座り、夜が形を変えるのを待つ。バッグの中のあるものは、もう彼の名前がついている。

ev_board.en: Flyers, lost cats, a poem someone pinned up and never claimed. You take what you need and leave the poem.
ev_board.ja: チラシ、迷い猫、誰かが貼って取りに来なかった詩。必要なものだけ取って、詩は残していく。

ev_stall.en: The flower seller wraps a single stem for you without asking who it is for.
ev_stall.ja: 花売りは誰に贈るのかも聞かずに、一輪だけ包んでくれる。

ev_kiosk.en: A late paper, a bus pass top-up, a mint. The city keeps its small promises.
ev_kiosk.ja: 遅い新聞、バス定期のチャージ、ミントひとつ。街は小さな約束を守る。

ev_heat_gate.en: Whatever happens next is a question, and he asks it out loud. You can say yes. You can say not tonight. Both are allowed.
ev_heat_gate.ja: 次に起きることは問いかけで、彼はそれを声に出して尋ねる。はいと言ってもいい。今夜はやめておくと言ってもいい。どちらも許されている。

ev_heat_locked.en: (Trust is not high enough yet for this — the scene stays closed, and so does nothing else. You can still say not tonight.)
ev_heat_locked.ja: （まだ信頼が足りない — この場面は閉じたまま。他に失うものはない。「今夜はやめておく」はいつでも選べる。）

ev_trust_missed.en: He let you in — but you got there the long way round, and the distance is still in the room. (Win a date with Distance under 60 for Trust.)
ev_trust_missed.ja: 彼は心を開いた — でも遠回りだった。距離はまだ部屋に残っている。（距離60未満で勝つと信頼が上がる）

ev_chapter_cg.ja: これは、ずっと覚えている。

ns_prologue.en: The evening star is up. Six doors in the city are still lit.
ns_prologue.ja: 宵の明星が昇った。街にはまだ灯りのついた扉が六つある。

ev_pro_1.en: Evening. The city switches its lights on one window at a time, and somewhere in it six men are still awake for reasons they have not told anyone.
ev_pro_1.ja: 夜。街は窓ひとつずつ灯りを点けていく。そのどこかで、六人の男が誰にも言っていない理由で、まだ起きている。

ev_pro_2.en: Everyone you will meet tonight is an adult, and so are you. Nothing happens here that is not asked for and answered yes.
ev_pro_2.ja: 今夜出会う人はみな大人で、あなたもそう。ここでは、尋ねられ「はい」と答えられたこと以外は何も起きない。

ev_pro_3.en: Whose night do you walk into?

ev_route_joined.en: You step out into the evening. He doesn't know yet that you are on your way.
ev_route_joined.ja: あなたは夜へ踏み出す。彼はまだ、あなたが向かっていることを知らない。

pre_doorman.en: A doorman with an earpiece and a clipboard steps into your path. "Name? You're not on the list."
pre_doorman.ja: イヤーピースとクリップボードのドアマンが行く手を塞ぐ。「お名前は？ リストにありませんね」

post_doorman.en: He checks the list again, finds a reason to have made a mistake, and holds the door. "Have a good night, miss."
post_doorman.ja: 彼はリストを見直し、自分の間違いだった理由を見つけて、扉を押さえる。「良い夜を」

pre_paparazzo.en: A flash goes off in your face. A man with a long lens grins. "Who are you to him? Give me a name and I'll make you famous."
pre_paparazzo.ja: 目の前でフラッシュが光る。望遠レンズの男がにやりと笑う。「彼とはどういう関係？ 名前をくれたら有名にしてやるよ」

post_paparazzo.en: He lowers the camera, deletes the frame in front of you, and goes to stand somewhere else.
post_paparazzo.ja: 彼はカメラを下ろし、あなたの目の前でその一枚を消して、別の場所へ立ち去る。

pre_columnist.en: A woman in a trench coat falls into step beside you, phone already recording. "Off the record — how long has this been going on?"
pre_columnist.ja: トレンチコートの女があなたの横に並ぶ。スマホはもう録音中。「オフレコで — いつから続いてるの？」

post_columnist.en: She stops the recording, looks at you for a long second, and laughs. "Fine. Keep it. Some things are better not printed."
post_columnist.ja: 彼女は録音を止め、しばらくあなたを見て、笑う。「いいわ。取っておきなさい。書かないほうがいいこともある」

bark_doorman_1.en: "I don't make the list. I just read it."
bark_doorman_1.ja: 「リストを作るのは俺じゃない。読むだけだ」

bark_doorman_2.ja: 彼はゆっくりとクリップボードを叩く。

bark_doorman_3.en: "Lot of people say they know him."
bark_doorman_3.ja: 「彼の知り合いだって言う人は多いんですよ」

bark_paparazzo_1.ja: 「一枚だけ笑って。読者のために」

bark_paparazzo_2.en: The shutter clicks three times, fast.
bark_paparazzo_2.ja: シャッターが三度、素早く鳴る。

bark_paparazzo_3.en: "Everyone's for sale, sweetheart. What's your price?"
bark_paparazzo_3.ja: 「誰にだって値段はあるさ。あんたのは？」

bark_columnist_1.en: "I'll find out anyway. Better from you."
bark_columnist_1.ja: 「どうせ調べはつくの。あなたから聞いたほうがいい」

bark_columnist_2.en: She smiles like she has already written the headline.
bark_columnist_2.ja: 彼女はもう見出しを書き終えたような顔で微笑む。

bark_columnist_3.ja: 「あなたがこんなに面白い人だって、彼は知ってるの？」

hb_open_1.en: He left the thread open. He was hoping.
hb_open_1.ja: 彼は話の糸を切らずにおいた。期待していたのだ。

hb_open_2.en: You're back, and it's late, and he noticed both.
hb_open_2.ja: あなたは戻ってきた。夜も遅い。彼はその両方に気づいている。

hb_read_1.en: One more word and he says it out loud.
hb_read_1.ja: あとひと言で、彼はそれを口にする。

hb_read_2.en: He's right at the edge of asking.
hb_read_2.ja: 彼は今にも尋ねそうだ。

hb_win_1.en: He'll think about that all night.
hb_win_1.ja: 彼は一晩中、そのことを考えるだろう。

hb_win_2.en: That landed. You can feel him go still.
hb_win_2.ja: 届いた。彼が静かになるのが分かる。

hb_win_3.en: Something just shifted, and you both felt it.
hb_win_3.ja: 何かが動いた。二人ともそれを感じた。

vb_stage_1.en: Something in him just gave way.
vb_stage_1.ja: 彼の中で何かがほどけた。

vb_stage_2.en: He stopped pretending he wasn't waiting.
vb_stage_2.ja: 彼は待っていないふりをやめた。

vb_stage_3.en: He's telling you the thing he doesn't tell anyone.
vb_stage_3.ja: 彼は誰にも言わないことを、あなたに話している。

vb_stage_4.en: You're not being careful any more. Neither is he.
vb_stage_4.ja: あなたはもう慎重じゃない。彼もそう。

vb_win_big_1.en: He kept every word you ever gave him. All of them.
vb_win_big_1.ja: 彼はあなたがくれた言葉を全部取っておいた。ひとつ残らず。

vb_win_big_2.en: You reached the end of him, and he stayed.
vb_win_big_2.ja: あなたは彼のいちばん奥まで辿り着き、彼はそこに留まった。

vb_unlock_1.en: A new chapter just opened for you.
vb_unlock_1.ja: 新しい章があなたのために開いた。

vb_unlock_2.en: Someone else has been waiting his turn.
vb_unlock_2.ja: 別の誰かが、自分の番を待っていた。

vb_streak_1.en: Three in a row. You know exactly what he needs.
vb_streak_1.ja: 三連続。彼に何が必要か、あなたはもう分かっている。

vb_streak_2.en: You're reading him like you wrote him.
vb_streak_2.ja: まるで自分で書いた人物のように、彼を読めている。

vb_fail_1.en: He's gone quiet. Let him have the moment.
vb_fail_1.ja: 彼は黙り込んだ。その時間を彼にあげて。

vb_fail_2.en: That one missed. Say it another way.
vb_fail_2.ja: 今のは外れ。別の言い方で。

vb_idle_1.en: He's still on the other end of this.
vb_idle_1.ja: 彼はまだ、この向こう側にいる。

vb_idle_2.ja: まだ起きてる？ 彼もよ。

bark_hold_guyan_1.en: He nods, slowly, the way he does when he is memorising something.
bark_hold_guyan_1.ja: 彼はゆっくりと頷く。何かを覚えようとする時の仕草だ。

bark_hold_guyan_2.en: "Take your time," he says. "The rain isn't in a hurry either."
bark_hold_guyan_2.ja: 「ゆっくりでいいよ」と彼は言う。「雨も急いでないから」

bark_hold_guyan_3.en: Dango settles between you, and he takes that as permission to stay quiet a while.
bark_hold_guyan_3.ja: 団子が二人のあいだに落ち着く。彼はそれを、しばらく黙っていていい許しだと受け取る。

bark_hold_guyan_4.en: "I'd like to hear the rest of that," he says, and goes pink at his own boldness.
bark_hold_guyan_4.ja: 「その続きを聞きたいな」と彼は言い、自分の大胆さに頬を染める。

bark_hold_ethan_1.en: He doesn't fill the silence. He lets it sit, and watches what you do with it.
bark_hold_ethan_1.ja: 彼は沈黙を埋めない。ただそこに置き、あなたがそれをどうするかを見ている。

bark_hold_ethan_2.en: "Keep going," he says. "I'm not going anywhere tonight."
bark_hold_ethan_2.ja: 「続けて」と彼は言う。「今夜はどこにも行かない」

bark_hold_ethan_3.en: He turns the glass a quarter turn on the table and doesn't drink from it.
bark_hold_ethan_3.ja: 彼はグラスを机の上で四分の一回転させ、口はつけない。

bark_hold_ethan_4.en: "Say that again," he says. "Slower. I want to be sure I heard it."
bark_hold_ethan_4.ja: 「もう一度言って」と彼は言う。「ゆっくり。聞き間違いじゃないか確かめたい」

bark_hold_luxingye_1.en: He drops his chin onto the back of the chair and grins up at you. "Go on. I'm listening."
bark_hold_luxingye_1.ja: 彼は椅子の背にあごを乗せて、にっと見上げる。「どうぞ。聞いてるよ」

bark_hold_luxingye_2.en: "You know nobody talks to me like this," he says. "Don't stop on my account."
bark_hold_luxingye_2.ja: 「こんなふうに話しかけてくる人、いないんだ」と彼は言う。「俺のために止めないで」

bark_hold_luxingye_3.en: He plays two notes, stops, and looks at you instead of the strings.
bark_hold_luxingye_3.ja: 彼は二音だけ弾いて止め、弦ではなくあなたを見る。

bark_hold_luxingye_4.en: "Say more things," he says. "I like your voice better than the room."
bark_hold_luxingye_4.ja: 「もっと話して」と彼は言う。「この部屋より、君の声のほうが好きだ」

bark_hold_liam_1.en: He leans back against the tailgate and gives you his whole attention, which is a lot of attention.
bark_hold_liam_1.ja: 彼は荷台にもたれて、あなたに全部の注意を向ける。それはかなりの量の注意だ。

bark_hold_liam_2.en: "Keep talking," he says. "I've got nowhere I need to be till six."
bark_hold_liam_2.ja: 「話してて」と彼は言う。「六時まで、どこにも行く用はないから」

bark_hold_liam_3.en: Biscuit sighs and flops across both your feet, pinning you there.
bark_hold_liam_3.ja: ビスケットがため息をついて二人の足の上に寝転び、あなたをそこに留める。

bark_hold_liam_4.en: "That's the good stuff," he says. "Say the rest of it."
bark_hold_liam_4.ja: 「そこがいいとこなんだ」と彼は言う。「続きを言って」

bark_hold_adrian_1.en: He doesn't answer. He watches you, which from him is the same as answering.
bark_hold_adrian_1.ja: 彼は答えない。あなたを見ている。彼の場合、それが答えと同じだ。

bark_hold_adrian_2.en: "Don't stop," he says, short. "I'm not bored yet."
bark_hold_adrian_2.ja: 「止めるな」と彼は短く言う。「まだ飽きてない」

bark_hold_adrian_3.en: He mutes the strings with his palm so he can hear you better, and pretends he didn't.
bark_hold_adrian_3.ja: 彼は手のひらで弦を押さえて、あなたの声がよく聞こえるようにする。そして、そうしなかったふりをする。

bark_hold_adrian_4.en: "Again," he says. "That part. Say it again."
bark_hold_adrian_4.ja: 「もう一回」と彼は言う。「そこ。もう一回言って」

bark_hold_fushen_1.en: He says nothing. The silence is not a wall this time; it is an invitation, and you can tell the difference now.
bark_hold_fushen_1.ja: 彼は何も言わない。今度の沈黙は壁ではなく招待で、あなたにはもうその違いが分かる。

bark_hold_fushen_2.en: "Continue," he says. It is the closest he gets to please.
bark_hold_fushen_2.ja: 「続けろ」と彼は言う。彼にとって「お願い」に最も近い言葉だ。

bark_hold_fushen_3.en: He sets his glass down without a sound and waits.
bark_hold_fushen_3.ja: 彼は音を立てずにグラスを置き、待つ。

bark_hold_fushen_4.en: "I'm listening," he says, and he is — completely, which from him is rare.
bark_hold_fushen_4.ja: 「聞いている」と彼は言う。そして本当に聞いている — 完全に。彼にしては珍しく。

guyan_c1_open.en: The wind-chime gives a soft note as you push the door. There's only one person inside — up a ladder, tidying the top shelf. He turns, pauses a beat, then says gently, "It's coming down hard out there. Take your time. No rush." An orange cat on the counter opens one eye at you, then goes back to sleep. He is thirty-three, you are thirty, and the shop keeps whatever hours the two of you decide it keeps.

guyan_c1_cast.en: Gu Yan, 33. The player character is 30. Both adults.

guyan_c1_b1_dango_ev.en: The orange cat, Dango, hops down and rubs against your ankle. He looks surprised. "That's… unusual. He won't even let me pick him up most days."

guyan_c1_b1_dango_he.en: "That's — unusual." He blinks at the cat winding round your ankle. "He doesn't do that. He doesn't do that for me, and I feed him." When you tease him about being outranked by his own cat, the tips of his ears go faintly pink. "He has opinions. Apparently he's decided."

guyan_c1_b2_book_ev.en: He pulls an old book of poems from the shelf, hesitates, then sets it by your hand. "This one… I could never quite bring myself to sell it. If you like it, keep it here for now."

guyan_c1_b2_book_he.en: He slides the book of poems to rest by your hand, as though it simply ended up there. "This one never sells," he says, which is a lie of omission; he has taken it off the shelf every time it nearly did. "Keep it here for now. If you like it. The third poem is the good one."

guyan_c1_b3_close_ev.en: The old clock strikes nine — long past closing. He glances at the sign on the door, but leaves the 'Open' placard as it is, unturned.

guyan_c1_b3_close_he.en: The clock strikes nine. He glances at the door sign and leaves it exactly as it is. When you point out the time he looks at the window instead of at you. "The rain hasn't let up," he says. "It would be unkind to send anyone out into that. The shop doesn't mind."

guyan_c1_c1a_q.en: You open the book of poems. On the flyleaf, a faded line in fountain pen. Watching you read it, he asks quietly, "…You found that line?"

guyan_c1_c1a_r0.en: The tips of his ears go pink. "I wrote it a long time ago… back when I didn't know who it was for yet."

guyan_c1_c1a_r1.en: He listens to the whole line in your voice, and for a long moment says nothing — just looks at you, as if hearing his own words for the first time.

guyan_c1_c1a_r2.en: He waves his hands, flustered. "It's not — that one's not for sale. I mean — just keep it, and read it. Please."

guyan_c1_c1b_q.en: The rain eases a little. He offers you an umbrella — then realizes it's the only one. "Take it," he says. "I live upstairs."

guyan_c1_c1b_r0.en: "…Alright." He presses his lips together, as if quietly filing away the words 'another day'.

guyan_c1_c1b_r1.en: He doesn't insist — just walks you to the door and stands under the lamp, watching until you're out of sight.

guyan_c1_c1b_r2.en: He blinks, as if no one has ever asked him back. "I… I'll be fine." He lowers his head and smiles, very softly.

guyan_c2_open.en: You come back with the umbrella. The chime rings, and he looks up from behind a stack of books — for a second his eyes brighten, then he quickly ducks his head and pretends to sort spines. "You came," he says, softer than he meant to. Dango has already claimed your usual chair.

guyan_c2_b1_tea_ev.en: He makes you tea — the osmanthus oolong you mentioned liking, once, in passing. He says nothing about it, just slides the cup across.

guyan_c2_b1_tea_he.en: He slides the cup across without a word — osmanthus oolong, which you mentioned once, weeks ago, in passing. When you notice, he busies himself with the pot. "I had some. Lying around. It was going to go stale." The tin is new. He knows you can see that the tin is new.

guyan_c2_b2_shop_ev.en: "This shop was my grandfather's," he says suddenly, fingers tracing the grain of the counter. "After he passed, everyone told me to sell it. But every time I come in, it feels like he's just gone to the back to make tea."

guyan_c2_b2_shop_he.en: "It was my grandfather's." His fingers follow the grain of the counter, an old habit. "Everyone said sell it when he passed. But I come in in the morning and it's as if he's just gone to the back to make tea." Then, gently, closing the door: "You'd like the poetry shelf. Come."

guyan_c2_b3_note_ev.en: You notice many books here hold little slips of paper — notes he writes for future readers. One says: "If you've read this far, then all the time we missed was exactly enough to meet."

guyan_c2_b3_note_he.en: "Oh — those." He reaches for the slip and doesn't quite take it from you. "I write them for whoever gets there next. It's a foolish habit, I've never explained it to anyone." When you read one aloud he studies the floor intently. "...You weren't supposed to find that one so quickly."

guyan_c2_c2a_q.en: Watching you move through the shop, he asks suddenly, "Do you think… keeping an old bookshop like this is a waste of a life?"

guyan_c2_c2a_r0.en: His breath catches. He looks down, and it's a long while before he says, "…Then stay a little longer."

guyan_c2_c2a_r1.en: "…Thank you," he says quietly, as if he's waited years to hear it.

guyan_c2_c2a_r2.en: He looks toward the light in the window. "I used to not be sure. Now… I think I'm starting to be."

guyan_c2_c2b_q.en: As you leave he stops you, holding that slip of paper, hesitating. "This one… would you want to keep it?"

guyan_c2_c2b_r0.en: He hands it over, and his fingertips brush yours by accident. Neither of them dares move.

guyan_c2_c2b_r1.en: He looks away quickly. "…I didn't know you when I wrote it. But reading it now — it seems like I did."

guyan_c2_c2b_r2.en: "Next time," he repeats, and his eyes curve. "Alright. I'll be waiting."

guyan_c3_open.en: That night you got stranded across the city; the last bus was gone and the rain only grew. With no umbrella, you stood under a convenience-store awning, resigned to walking home soaked. Just as you'd given up — a figure came running through the downpour, hair and half his body drenched, umbrella in hand. It's him. "You posted you had no umbrella," he pants, pressing it into your hands. "…So I came."

guyan_c3_b1_umbrella_ev.en: He tilts the umbrella entirely toward you, his own shoulder out in the rain. You say he'll get soaked. He just smiles. "I'm fine — I'm hardier than I look. It's books that can't take the rain."

guyan_c3_b1_umbrella_he.en: "I'm fine. I'm hardier than I look — it's books that can't take the rain." He has tipped the umbrella so far toward you that his own shoulder is a dark soak, and he keeps it there when you push back. "No, leave it. You'll only make us both wet and then it was for nothing."

guyan_c3_b2_confess_edge_ev.en: At your building he stops. The rain is loud. He opens his mouth, then only manages: "I'm… not very good at saying these things…" The sentence trails off, but the tips of his ears have gone fully red.

guyan_c3_b2_confess_edge_he.en: "I'm — not very good at saying these things." The rain is loud on the awning and he has run out of sentence. His ears have gone entirely red. If you help him along he doesn't get any braver, only more honest, in pieces: "It's only — I'd rather you didn't go up yet. That's all it is."

guyan_c3_c3a_q.en: His unfinished sentence hangs in the rain. You can finish it for him, or wait. He looks at you — softly, and afraid.

guyan_c3_c3a_r0.en: His head snaps up. Rain slides off his lashes and he forgets to blink. "…You first," he says, almost holding his breath.

guyan_c3_c3a_r1.en: He draws a breath, voice barely there. "I think… every day I've been waiting for you to push that door open."

guyan_c3_c3a_r2.en: He blinks, then laughs, eyes a little wet. "…Why are you always the one worrying about me."

guyan_c3_c3b_q.en: It's time to part. He leaves the soaked umbrella with you and turns to walk back into the rain. You call out — do you invite him up to dry off?

guyan_c3_c3b_r0.en: He stops, hesitates a long moment, then nods gently. "…Just one cup. Until the rain lets up."

guyan_c3_c3b_r1.en: "Mm." He steps back into the rain, but keeps looking back at you, until he can't anymore.

guyan_c3_c3b_r2.en: He goes completely still; in the rain there's only the sound of two people breathing. "…This time," he says softly, "let me be the one to walk you back."

guyan_c4_open.en: You push the door open and the air is wrong. He sits behind the counter, a letter in hand. The whole street is being redeveloped; the shop's lease is up, and the developer's offer is generous. "They say… it's the sensible choice," he says evenly — but you see his knuckles gone white around the paper.

guyan_c4_b1_letter_ev.en: He slides the letter toward you. Signing it means he'll never again have to worry about a bookshop that only loses money. But he hasn't said one word about signing.

guyan_c4_b1_letter_he.en: "They'd clear the debt and then some." He states it like a stock figure. "Every sensible person I know says take it." Only when you ask what he wants does it come out at all, quietly: "I don't want to let it go. That's not an argument. It's just the truth of it."

guyan_c4_b2_boxes_ev.en: He begins, silently, to box up the books. When he reaches the book of poems from the day you met, his hand stops — and for a long while, it doesn't go into the box.

guyan_c4_b2_boxes_he.en: He packs in silence because packing looks like deciding. Then his hand stops over the poetry book from the evening you walked in, and stays stopped. "...I can't put this one in," he says, and his voice isn't steady. "I've tried twice. I keep finding it back on the counter."

guyan_c4_bx_after_hours_ev.en: The boxes stay unpacked on the shop floor. He turns the sign to Closed for the first time in the whole story, and he is very careful about the lock, because his hands are not steady.

guyan_c4_bx_after_hours_he.en: "I want to say it properly, so I'm going to say it slowly." His ears are scarlet and his voice is level, which costs him. "I would like you to stay tonight. Not because of the shop, or the letter, or any of it. If you'd rather not, we'll make tea and I'll walk you home and I won't be any different tomorrow — I need you to believe that part before you answer." You answer. He closes his eyes for a second. Then he takes the poetry book off the counter, and puts it back on the shelf where it has always belonged, and turns off the lamp.

guyan_c4_c4a_q.en: He finally looks up. "Tell me… should I sign it?" It's the first time he's ever put a decision in someone else's hands.

guyan_c4_c4a_r0.en: His eyes go red at once; he turns his face away. "…I kept this place alone so long. It turns out 'I'll be with you' is all it took to hold it up."

guyan_c4_c4a_r1.en: "I'm on your side" — he repeats it under his breath, then sets the letter down.

guyan_c4_c4a_r2.en: He stares a long moment, then laughs softly. "…And inside you too. Right?"

guyan_c4_c4a_r3.en: "Tea," he says, visibly relieved to have something to do with his hands. "Yes. Tea I can manage."

guyan_c4_c4b_q.en: The book of poems is still stuck in his hand. He looks at you. "This one — I really can't put it away."

guyan_c4_c4b_r0.en: He hands it over, then suddenly closes his hand over yours, book and all. "Then can I… be yours too."

guyan_c4_c4b_r1.en: The book goes back where it belongs. He doesn't let go of your hand. "…So then — we're not moving out after all?"

guyan_c4_c4b_r2.en: He lowers his head, presses the book to his chest, and says very softly, "…Then it never goes in a box, as long as I live."

guyan_c5_open.en: The shop didn't move. He, a handful of old regulars, and you took it over together — and now a new sign hangs above the door, in his own hand. On opening day the sun is good and Dango sleeps in a warm patch. He sets the poetry book before you. Beneath the old faded line on the flyleaf, there's a new one, the ink not yet dry. "This line," he says, "I wrote this morning."

guyan_c5_b1_newline_ev.en: The new line reads: "I used to write for someone I wasn't sure would ever come. Now I know — she already has."

guyan_c5_b1_newline_he.en: He has written a second line under the old one on the flyleaf and he cannot look at you while you read it: *I used to write for someone I wasn't sure would ever come. Now I know — she already has.* "Don't read it aloud," he says, hopelessly. "Please. Just — read it."

guyan_c5_b2_ask_ev.en: He finally gathers his courage, voice a little unsteady. "That sentence I could never finish — will you… let me finish it today?"

guyan_c5_b2_ask_he.en: "That sentence I could never finish." He has rehearsed this and it is still unsteady. "Will you let me finish it today?" He waits for your yes before he says it, and when he says it there is no flourish at all — only a shy man saying a true thing, once, properly, and meaning every syllable.

guyan_c5_bx_morning_ev.en: Morning in the reopened shop. Dango has taken the warm patch. The new sign is still crooked.

guyan_c5_bx_morning_he.en: "I have been trying for an hour," he says, from somewhere near your hair, "to think of a line for the flyleaf, and everything I come up with is too pleased with itself." He gives up happily. "I'll just write the date. I'll know what it means."

guyan_c5_c5a_q.en: "Say it," you say softly. "I'm listening." He draws a breath —

guyan_c5_c5a_r0.en: He grips your hand and looks into your eyes. "I love you. From the moment you pushed that door open and Dango jumped down — all the way through every rainy day to come."

guyan_c5_c5a_r1.en: He freezes, then smiles, his eyes full of light. "Then… will you keep this shop with me — for a very, very long time?"

guyan_c5_c5a_r2.en: "…Then that's enough." He exhales, resting his forehead lightly against yours. "I was afraid I'd say it badly. But you understood all of it."

guyan_c5_c5a_r3.en: "...That's fair," he says softly. "That's more than fair. Sit down, then, and let me try again."

ethan_c1_open.en: The elevator stopped on the wrong floor. The whole level is dark except the office at the end of the hall — door open, a man standing with his back to you at the floor-to-ceiling window, tie loosened, the whiskey in his hand untouched. You are twenty-nine; he is thirty-eight, and neither of you is anywhere you have to be tomorrow.

ethan_c1_cast.en: Ethan Cole, 38. The player character is 29. Both adults.

ethan_c1_b1_call_ev.en: His phone lights up on the desk. He glances at it, declines the call, and looks at you properly for the first time.

ethan_c1_b1_call_he.en: "That was the chairman," he says, and doesn't elaborate. He sets the phone face-down. "He'll survive until Monday." Then he looks at you properly for the first time, the way a man looks at something he has decided to actually see. "You're still here."

ethan_c1_b2_blackout_ev.en: The building goes dark. Only the red glow of emergency lights, and the whole city outside the window.

ethan_c1_b2_blackout_he.en: "Generators take ninety seconds." His voice has dropped without his permission. He moves half a step closer, and offers no reason for it. "Don't move toward the desk, there's a chair leg. Just — stay where you are. I can hear you breathing, so I know where you are."

ethan_c1_b3_name_ev.en: He suddenly asks, 'What's your name?' — as if he just realized he never asked.

ethan_c1_b3_name_he.en: "What's your name?" It arrives out of nowhere, and he seems faintly annoyed at himself for not having asked. When you tell him, he repeats it once, quietly, the way he'd write something on a page he intends to keep. "All right. Now I know."

ethan_c1_c1_q.en: He sets the glass down and looks at you. "Why haven't you left?"

ethan_c1_c1_r0.en: A short laugh. "Then I owe the elevator."

ethan_c1_c1_r2.en: He raises an eyebrow and slides the second glass across to you.

ethan_c2_open.en: A week later, same floor. The door is closed this time, but he opens it almost instantly when you ring — as if he'd been waiting. There are two glasses on the table.

ethan_c2_b1_remember_ev.en: The drink he hands you is exactly the one you mentioned offhand last time.

ethan_c2_b1_remember_he.en: "They keep a case of it downstairs," he says, handing it over, which is not an answer and you both know it. He mentioned nothing, ordered nothing, and there it is. "Don't look at me like that. I have an excellent memory and very few uses for it."

ethan_c2_b2_why_here_ev.en: "My father was a security guard in this building for thirty years," he says suddenly, not looking at you.

ethan_c2_b2_why_here_he.en: "My father worked this building. Night shift, thirty years, that door to that door." He still isn't looking at you. "I bought it eleven years ago. Nobody here knows that, and I'd prefer it stayed that way." A beat. "Your glass is empty. Say something else."

ethan_c2_b3_interrupt_ev.en: An assistant knocks and comes in with papers, then visibly freezes when he sees you — he's never seen anyone up here with his boss.

ethan_c2_b3_interrupt_he.en: "Leave them on the desk. Goodnight." The door closes on a man who has never once seen anyone up here after ten. Ethan doesn't explain you to him, before or after. "He'll be insufferable about it by Wednesday," he says. "I find I don't mind."

ethan_c2_c2_q.en: He asks, "What do you think I am?" — and he isn't making small talk.

ethan_c2_c2_r0.en: He does not speak for a long moment. Then: "...No one has put it that way."

ethan_c2_c2_r1.en: "Control is a luxury," he says. "I can simply afford it."

ethan_c2_c2_r2.en: He smiles -- and this time it reaches his eyes.

ethan_c3_open.en: You changed plans to see an old friend, and it starts raining on the way back. Ducking into a noodle shop, you look up — he's in the corner, suit jacket over the chair, eating the most ordinary bowl of noodles. He sees you too.

ethan_c3_b1_umbrella_ev.en: The rain gets heavier. Walking out, he tilts the umbrella entirely over you — his whole right shoulder is soaked, but he says he's fine.

ethan_c3_b1_umbrella_he.en: "It's rain," he says, as if that settles it, the entire right side of his coat going dark. When you push the umbrella back toward him he pushes it back. "I'm not being gallant. I'm being efficient. One of us dry is better arithmetic than two of us damp."

ethan_c3_b2_photo_ev.en: An old photo falls out of his wallet: a man in a security uniform, and a skinny teenager.

ethan_c3_b2_photo_he.en: He picks it up faster than he needs to. Then, because you saw: "That's him. That's me, at fifteen." A long pause, and he gives you the short version because the short version is all he can carry. "He worked nights so I wouldn't have to. That's the whole story."

ethan_c3_c3_q.en: Standing in the rain as you part, he says suddenly, "I'm flying to Tokyo Wednesday."

ethan_c3_c3_r0.en: He nods, and says nothing more.

ethan_c3_c3_r1.en: A long silence. Then: "...I don't know either."

ethan_c3_c3_r2.en: He goes still. The rain keeps falling. He does not move.

ethan_c4_open.en: The gala for the closed acquisition. He's on stage, flawless. Someone beside you says quietly, "He cut loose his own partner. What do you think you are to him?" — and they're holding a document.

ethan_c4_b1_accusation_ev.en: The document bears his signature, dated three years ago — he did cut his co-founder loose during a crisis.

ethan_c4_b1_accusation_he.en: "It's my signature and it's the right date." No defence, no preamble. Only when you ask him straight does the rest come, flat and complete: "The bank would have taken his house. I couldn't stop the vote. So I paid his debts for two years through a third party and let him hate me instead. He still does."

ethan_c4_b2_leave_ev.en: He steps off the stage and walks straight across the entire room toward you — every camera follows.

ethan_c4_b2_leave_he.en: He crosses the entire room to you with every lens in the building following, and stops close enough that there is nothing else to call it. "They'll run this everywhere by morning," he says. "I'd like you to know I did the arithmetic on the stairs, and I walked down them anyway."

ethan_c4_bx_after_hours_ev.en: The car doesn't go to your building. Neither of you says anything about that until the lift doors close on the forty-first floor.

ethan_c4_bx_after_hours_he.en: "I'm going to say this badly." He hasn't let go of your hand since the gala floor. "I have spent eleven years being extremely careful about what I want, and I'd like to stop, tonight, with you, if that's something you also want. Say no and I'll take you home and nothing about tomorrow changes." You don't say no. He exhales like a man setting down something heavy, and the last thing you see before the lights go is the city, forty-one floors down, doing its work without either of you.

ethan_c4_c4_q.en: He stops in front of you. "Ask me. Right now."

ethan_c4_c4_r0.en: "It's real," he says. "But it isn't all of it. Will you hear the rest?"

ethan_c4_c4_r1.en: He glances at the cameras around you, and nods. "...Thank you."

ethan_c4_c4_r2.en: Something in his face gives, just for a second -- like no one has believed him without asking in a very long time.

ethan_c4_c4_r3.en: "Then we'll stay here," he says, and means it entirely. "I've got a whole city and no plans. Sit down."

ethan_c5_open.en: He turns off every light on the floor. The city's glow floods in through the glass. "My father loved this hour on his night shifts," he says. "I never understood why. I do now."

ethan_c5_b1_offer_ev.en: "The board wants me in New York. Three years." A pause. "I haven't answered them."

ethan_c5_b1_offer_he.en: "New York. Three years, running the whole region." He turns the glass and doesn't drink. "I haven't answered them." He doesn't say why he hasn't. He looks at you and lets the silence do the asking, because he has never learned to do it himself.

ethan_c5_b2_truth_ev.en: He finally turns around. "Everything I've ever taken, I never actually wanted."

ethan_c5_b2_truth_he.en: He turns around at last. "Everything I've ever taken, I never actually wanted." He doesn't soften it, doesn't dress it, doesn't follow it with anything clever. He is simply standing there, out of armour, in the dark of his own building. "That's the whole sentence. I've never said it out loud before."

ethan_c5_bx_morning_ev.en: Six a.m. The top-floor light is off for the first time in eleven years, and he is still asleep.

ethan_c5_bx_morning_he.en: He wakes up slowly, which you would not have thought he knew how to do. "Don't," he says, when you reach for your phone, and pulls you back under his arm without opening his eyes. "Nine minutes. The building has survived worse." It is the most extravagant thing you have ever watched him spend.

ethan_c5_c5_q.en: "So what do you want now?" — you're the one asking.

ethan_c5_c5_r0.en: He crosses the room, slowly. "I want a reason to stay in this city."

ethan_c5_c5_r1.en: "I want you," he says, quietly. "This is the one thing I don't want to calculate."

ethan_c5_c5_r2.en: He is still for a long time. Then, a small smile. "...All right."

ethan_c5_c5_r3.en: "Slower," he agrees. "I've never been any good at slow. I'd like to find out if I can be."

luxingye_c1_open.en: Holding a mis-issued staff pass, you get waved backstage by security in the confusion. Round a corner — and there he is: in-ears out, makeup a little smudged, hugging his knees on a prop crate, secretly eating a convenience-store rice ball. He sees you and jumps; the rice ball nearly hits the floor. "…Th-that thing you just saw — can we pretend it didn't happen?" He is twenty-seven, you are twenty-six, and the only person waiting up for either of you tonight is the other one.

luxingye_c1_cast.en: Lu Xingye, 27. The player character is 26. Both adults.

luxingye_c1_b1_riceball_ev.en: He tries to hide the rice ball behind his back — and smears sauce on his cheek. He hasn't noticed, and is still valiantly trying to project top-idol composure.

luxingye_c1_b1_riceball_he.en: "Okay. Okay!" He shoves the rice ball behind his back and lifts his chin like a man with dignity, sauce on his cheek. "You saw nothing. Nation's top idol, impeccable diet, photographed for magazines." A beat. "...There's a second one in the bag. It's yours if you never speak of this."

luxingye_c1_b2_deal_ev.en: "Tell you what," he leans in suddenly, eyes bright, "you keep my secret, and I'll… show you a side of me nobody else has seen. Deal?"

luxingye_c1_b2_deal_he.en: "Tell you what." He leans in, bright-eyed, all mischief on the surface. "Your silence, and I show you a version of me that hasn't been on a single broadcast. Fair trade." He says it like a game. He is, quietly, hoping very much that you say yes, and he would deny that under oath.

luxingye_c1_b3_name_ev.en: Staff outside are calling his name, rushing him. He doesn't move — instead he asks, "…And you? What's your name? I want to remember who's keeping my secret."

luxingye_c1_b3_name_he.en: Someone outside is shouting his name for the third time and he does not move. "Hang on, hang on — what's yours? I can't have a secret-keeper I can't file under anything." You tell him, and he repeats it once, grinning, tasting it. "Right. Noted. Permanently."

luxingye_c1_c1a_q.en: He tilts his head, grinning wickedly. "Name your price for silence. Autograph? Selfie? Or… me?"

luxingye_c1_c1a_r0.en: He touches his cheek, yelps 'AH' and leaps up, ears scarlet. "Wh— why didn't you SAY something!"

luxingye_c1_c1a_r1.en: He blinks, then gets more into it, not less. "Oh? Not a fan? Then I'll just have to make you one."

luxingye_c1_c1a_r2.en: His mouth opens; for once he has no comeback. He looks away and mutters, "…Not many people want to see the offstage me."

luxingye_c1_c1b_q.en: Staff are calling again. He stands, but turns back at the door. "I've got another appearance after this. You… gonna leave?"

luxingye_c1_c1b_r0.en: He arches a brow, flashing his signature pre-stage smile. "Then watch closely. This one's for you."

luxingye_c1_c1b_r1.en: "Row seven," he repeats, like jotting down a coordinate. "…Alright. Noted."

luxingye_c1_c1b_r2.en: His smile dims a little; he waves. "…Right. Well. The secret — I'm counting on you."

luxingye_c2_open.en: He messages you to come to the rehearsal room — from a private, unverified account no fan knows exists. When you arrive, the huge room has a single lamp on, and he's alone on the floor with a guitar, makeup off, in an ordinary hoodie. "You came," he says, looking up with a smile completely unlike the one on stage — soft, and a little tired.

luxingye_c2_b1_song_ev.en: He idly plays a melody — soft, lovely, unreleased. "This bit… is something I wrote myself. The label says it's not 'commercial' enough."

luxingye_c2_b1_song_he.en: "This bit's mine. I wrote it." The melody wanders on under his hands, unhurried. "Label says it's not commercial. They're probably right, they usually are." He's watching your face while pretending not to. "...You can say if it's bad. People don't, and it makes me insane."

luxingye_c2_b2_cage_ev.en: "You know," he says, hugging his knees, "the last time anyone asked if I was tired was three years ago. Everyone only asks if I'm 'in good form today'."

luxingye_c2_b2_cage_he.en: "Three years since anyone asked if I was tired," he says, chin on his knees, light as a shrug. "They ask if I'm in good form. Different question." Then, immediately, because being seen makes his skin itch: "Anyway — tragic idol backstory, very on-brand, please clap."

luxingye_c2_b3_photo_ev.en: His phone lights up — a trending topic: '#LuXingye's late-night secret rendezvous'. He glances at it, but watches your reaction first.

luxingye_c2_b3_photo_he.en: He tilts the screen so you can read the trending tag, watching you and not it. "Late-night secret rendezvous. They'll have me engaged by Thursday." A grin that's doing a lot of work. "This is the part where most people remember an early morning. I'm just saying. In case you were about to."

luxingye_c2_c2a_q.en: He sets down the guitar and looks at you seriously. "Are you going to… one day only want the me that's on stage, too?"

luxingye_c2_c2a_r0.en: He freezes, then hides his face behind the guitar, voice muffled. "…Say things like that and I'll actually believe them."

luxingye_c2_c2a_r1.en: He lifts his eyes, lashes flickering. "…Then don't ever stop knowing this one."

luxingye_c2_c2a_r2.en: He bursts out laughing. "I will! Every single day, right in front of you!"

luxingye_c2_c2b_q.en: The rumor is still trending. He flips the phone face-down on the floor and asks, testing, "All this… doesn't scare you?"

luxingye_c2_c2b_r0.en: His eyes light up; he forces a casual tone. "Oh—— so you admit it." But his ears go red.

luxingye_c2_c2b_r1.en: He exhales and leans back against the wall. "…With that, I'll actually sleep tonight."

luxingye_c2_c2b_r2.en: He pauses, softening. "…You worried about me first. Fine — this is one kind of trouble I don't mind."

luxingye_c3_open.en: The final night of the tour, packed to the rafters. The lights fall; thousands of glow-sticks become a galaxy. You're in row seven — the seat he set aside for you. On the last encore, after the whole crowd's sing-along ends, he suddenly signals the band to stop. The arena goes silent; tens of thousands hold their breath. Mic in hand, he walks slowly to the edge of the stage, his gaze passing over the front rows to land on row seven — on you.

luxingye_c3_b1_song_for_you_ev.en: "This last song," he tells the whole arena, but his eyes are on you, "the label said it wasn't commercial enough to release. But tonight, I want to sing it for one person." — It's the unreleased song he played you in the rehearsal room.

luxingye_c3_b1_song_for_you_he.en: "This last one," he tells forty thousand people, and it is not forty thousand people he's telling, "the label said it wasn't commercial enough to put out." His hand isn't quite steady on the mic. "So tonight I'm going to sing it for one person, and they know who they are."

luxingye_c3_b2_confession_ev.en: As the last note fades, he doesn't take his usual bow. He looks straight at row seven, his voice echoing through the arena: "The person in row seven — I don't care how many headlines this makes tomorrow. I like you." First dead silence, then a tsunami of screams.

luxingye_c3_b2_confession_he.en: He doesn't bow. The last note is still ringing and he is looking at row seven with the whole arena holding its breath. "The person in row seven." His voice cracks the arena open. "I don't care how many headlines this makes tomorrow. I like you." Then silence. Then a tsunami.

luxingye_c3_c3a_q.en: Tens of thousands of eyes follow his gaze. Phone cameras swing to row seven. He stands on stage, waiting for an answer — how do you respond?

luxingye_c3_c3a_r0.en: He grins on stage like an idiot; tens of thousands scream along. Into the mic, voice shaking, he says, "…She said yes."

luxingye_c3_c3a_r1.en: The arena detonates. He covers his face and crouches down, shoulders trembling — and that's not a performance; he's actually crying.

luxingye_c3_c3a_r2.en: He understands the nod. Under the lights, he mouths, silently, just for you: 'thank you'.

luxingye_c3_c3b_q.en: After the show he rushes to row seven, breathless, eyes still red. "Just now… was that too reckless? Will you hate me for exposing you?"

luxingye_c3_c3b_r0.en: He pulls you into a hug, buries his face in your neck. "…The one reckless thing I'll never regret."

luxingye_c3_c3b_r1.en: His nose stings. "…You're the first person to be happy for that song."

luxingye_c3_c3b_r2.en: He laughs through the tears and bumps his forehead to yours. "Great. Now I'll only get more reckless — for you."

luxingye_c4_open.en: The confession clip hits hundreds of millions of views overnight. Some fans cheer, some leave; the label is furious. Summoned to the company, you see him through the glass door, alone at the head of the long table, surrounded by executives applying pressure. One holds termination clauses; another slides over a statement — if he publicly says it was 'just a stage gimmick', it all blows over. Through the glass, he sees you.

luxingye_c4_b1_statement_ev.en: An executive pushes the statement in front of him, pen extended. Sign it, and his career is untouched. He stares at the page and doesn't move.

luxingye_c4_b1_statement_he.en: The statement says it was a stage gimmick. The pen is being held out. He looks at it for a long moment and does not take it. "They want me to say it was a bit," he says, to you, not to them, and very quietly. "I'm not going to say it was a bit."

luxingye_c4_b2_walk_ev.en: He suddenly stands, pushes open the boardroom door, and — in front of every executive — walks straight toward you outside the glass. The whole room falls silent.

luxingye_c4_b2_walk_he.en: He stands up mid-sentence, walks out through the glass door, and crosses to you in front of every executive who has ever owned a piece of him. "That's it. That's the whole meeting." He's shaking slightly and grinning like an idiot. "Ask me later if it was worth it. I'll say yes."

luxingye_c4_bx_after_hours_ev.en: The car is a decoy and the flat is borrowed and nobody on earth knows where either of you is. He locks the door and puts his back against it, laughing, out of breath.

luxingye_c4_bx_after_hours_he.en: "Okay. Okay." He's grinning and it keeps slipping into something less practised. "Full disclosure: I've been famous since I was nineteen and I have no idea how to do this part without it being a bit. So tell me if it's too fast, tell me if you want to just eat noodles and sit on the floor, tell me anything —" You tell him. He stops talking, which almost never happens, and the borrowed flat is very quiet for a long time after that.

luxingye_c4_c4a_q.en: He stops in front of you, the fuming executives at his back. "They want me to say it was fake. Tell me — should I sign?"

luxingye_c4_c4a_r0.en: His eyes go red, but he smiles. "'We.' …Best word I've heard in days."

luxingye_c4_c4a_r1.en: He pushes the statement back to the executives without looking. "You heard her. I'm not signing."

luxingye_c4_c4a_r2.en: He cuts you off instantly. "No. I can quit the industry. I can't quit you."

luxingye_c4_c4a_r3.en: "Oh thank God," he says, sliding down the door. "Noodles. I'm so much better at noodles."

luxingye_c4_c4b_q.en: An executive says coldly behind him, "Think hard, Lu Xingye. One step out that door and there's no going back." He doesn't turn — he just looks at you, waiting for a single look.

luxingye_c4_c4b_r0.en: He takes your hand without hesitation, then tells the executives over his shoulder, "Going back? I never planned to."

luxingye_c4_c4b_r1.en: He draws a breath and steps across the threshold, to your side.

luxingye_c4_c4b_r2.en: He grips your hand tighter and says, seriously, "You are the world I want."

luxingye_c5_open.en: The storm passed. He wasn't destroyed, and he didn't cave — after talks with the label collapsed, he simply started his own small studio and sings what he wants. Tonight is his first show as an independent artist, in a livehouse that seats a few dozen. No sea of glow-sticks, no trending topics. You're still in row seven — except tonight, the whole place barely has a row eight. He steps up with his guitar and finds you at once.

luxingye_c5_b1_new_song_ev.en: "This song," he says, tuning a string, "is a new one I wrote after that last one. It's called 'Row Seven'." The few dozen people go quiet, and he begins to sing — every line is about you.

luxingye_c5_b1_new_song_he.en: "New one," he says, tuning a string. "It's called Row Seven." Forty people go quiet instead of forty thousand, and he prefers it. Every line is you. He sings it straight at you and doesn't perform a single bar of it, which is the most naked he has ever been on a stage.

luxingye_c5_b2_ask_forever_ev.en: The song ends. He sets down the guitar, steps off the little stage, and — in front of a few dozen watching people — kneels on one knee on the floor before you. "I confessed to you in front of tens of thousands. Today, in front of a few dozen, I want to ask you something more important."

luxingye_c5_b2_ask_forever_he.en: He sets the guitar down, steps off the little stage and goes down on one knee on a floor that is definitely sticky. "I said it to tens of thousands. Now I'm asking something bigger in front of about forty." His hands are unsteady. "I gave up the empire. I'd like to keep you."

luxingye_c5_bx_morning_ev.en: Morning. No call time, no car, no manager. He has been awake for an hour and has not once picked up his phone.

luxingye_c5_bx_morning_he.en: "I worked out what's different," he says into your shoulder. "Nobody's waiting for me to come out and be someone." He thinks about it. "Terrifying. Ten out of ten. I'd like to do it every day for a while and then see."

luxingye_c5_c5a_q.en: He kneels before you, a few dozen eyes on you both, his voice trembling a little. "I want to sing 'Row Seven' for the rest of my life. Will you sit in that seat — for the rest of yours?"

luxingye_c5_c5a_r0.en: He freezes a beat, then laughs and pulls you into his arms. "Deal! From today, there's always a spot on my stage for you."

luxingye_c5_c5a_r1.en: He buries his face in your palm, shoulders shaking. "…Thank you — for still sitting there when I was nobody."

luxingye_c5_c5a_r2.en: The whole room cheers. Forehead to yours, he grins like a kid who stole candy. "This is the best show I'll ever play."

luxingye_c5_c5a_r3.en: "Deal." He grins, and for once it's the unrehearsed one. "I'm very good at waiting. I'll be terrible at it. Both things are true."

liam_c1_open.en: Your first day in the new place, a cardboard box gives out on the doorstep and your things scatter everywhere. As you scramble, a whistle comes from the yard next door — a broad-shouldered man walks over, one end of the couch you couldn't budge tucked easily under his arm, and grins. "New neighbor? I'm Liam. Relax — this kind of thing's my whole job." A golden retriever at his heels wags its tail and comes over to lick your hand. He is thirty-four, you are thirty-one, and the fence between the two yards is the only thing either of you answers to.

liam_c1_cast.en: Liam Reyes, 34. The player character is 31. Both adults.

liam_c1_b1_dog_ev.en: The golden retriever trots up with one of your dropped socks and drops it proudly at your feet. Liam laughs, shaking his head. "That's Biscuit, my partner. He's way more enthusiastic about fetching than firefighting."

liam_c1_b1_dog_he.en: "That's Biscuit. My partner." He takes the sock off him with an apologetic grin. "Way more enthusiastic about fetching than firefighting, which is a problem, since that's the job." He says *the job* the way other people say *the bus* — no weight on it. "Station's six blocks that way."

liam_c1_b2_fix_ev.en: He glances at your dripping faucet, and without a word digs a toolbox out of the truck. "That's a five-minute job. Sit down, have a root beer." — he's fixing it before you can even ask.

liam_c1_b2_fix_he.en: The toolbox is out of the truck before you've finished the sentence about the faucet. "Five-minute job. Sit down, have a root beer." When you thank him he waves it off with the wrench still in his hand. "Can't have my neighbour's sink haunting me. I'm between shifts, I've got nothing but time till six."

liam_c1_b3_call_ev.en: His pager goes off. He stands, his face turning a shade more serious. "Sorry — call-out with the crew." Before he goes, he looks back. "…What was your name again? I want to remember whose faucet I fixed."

liam_c1_b3_call_he.en: The pager goes and his face changes a shade — not dramatic, just *on*. "Sorry. Call-out with the crew." He's three steps away when he turns back. "Hey — what was your name again? I'd like to know whose faucet I fixed." You tell him. He repeats it once, grinning, and goes.

liam_c1_c1a_q.en: He hands you a root beer and sits on the tailgate. "So — what brings you out here on your own? Big city wear you out?"

liam_c1_c1a_r0.en: His ears go a little red as he laughs. "Careful — say stuff like that and I'll fix everything you own."

liam_c1_c1a_r1.en: His grin softens; he looks at her seriously. "…Then let's make this one stick. Home's easier with good neighbors."
