adrian_c5_open.en: The label really did drop him. But he doesn't look like a man who lost anything — he records himself, releases himself, and in a tiny underground livehouse that seats a few dozen, sings what he actually wants to. Tonight, that song gets its first full performance, his way. No rewrites, no collab. Just a few dozen people who came only to listen. You're in the front. He cradles the guitar and finds you at once. "Finished it," he says into the mic, looking only at you. "took me this long because I needed to know how it ends. …Turns out that part was up to you."

adrian_c5_b1_finished_ev.en: He plays the song, and this time it has a complete final verse. After the chorus, he adds a new line no one has ever heard: 'and for the first time, I wrote a song I don't wanna keep to myself.' On that line, he lifts his eyes to you.

adrian_c5_b1_finished_he.en: The song has a last verse now. After the chorus comes a line no one in the world has heard: *and for the first time, I wrote a song I don't wanna keep to myself.* On that line he lifts his eyes off the fretboard and puts them on you and leaves them there.

adrian_c5_b2_ask_ev.en: The song ends. He sets down the guitar, steps off the little stage, and — in front of a few dozen watching people — stands before you, rare and undefended. "I spent years hiding how I feel inside songs and denying every word. I'm done denying. So — plainly, no guitar, no lyrics to hide behind: I'm yours. …Are you mine?"

adrian_c5_b2_ask_he.en: He sets the guitar down and comes off the stage with nothing in his hands, which for him is the whole point. "I spent years hiding it in songs and denying every word. I'm done denying." No swagger left anywhere. "So — plainly. No guitar. I'm yours. Are you mine?"

adrian_c5_bx_morning_ev.en: Late morning. The guitar has not come out of its case. He has let it sit there for nine hours, which is a record.

adrian_c5_bx_morning_he.en: "I woke up and I didn't want to write anything," he says, faintly appalled. "Just — wanted to be in the room." He considers this. "Don't tell the band. They'll think I'm ill."

adrian_c5_c5a_q.en: He stands before you, a few dozen eyes on you both, undefended for once, waiting for your answer.

adrian_c5_c5a_r0.en: He laughs and pulls her in, forehead to hers, his voice trembling. "Deal. Every song from here on out — we finish it together."

adrian_c5_c5a_r1.en: He buries his face in her neck, shoulders shaking, deaf to the cheering of the room. "…no more denying. Not one word. I swear."

adrian_c5_c5a_r2.en: The room detonates with cheers. Forehead to hers, he smiles with no defenses at all. "…best encore I've ever played."

adrian_c5_c5a_r3.en: "I'll say it every day for a week," he says, short. "You'll get sick of it before I do."

fushen_c1_open.en: A dinner you were never meant to attend. After the guests left, you got lost on the terrace and wandered into a quiet study. He stands at the floor-to-ceiling window, back to you, a barely-touched glass of wine in hand. "The door is behind you," he says without turning, voice flat. "If you're here to hand me a business card, don't bother." He is thirty-six, you are thirty, and for once there is no one in this house but the two of you.

fushen_c1_cast.en: Fu Shen, 36. The player character is 30. Both adults.

fushen_c1_b1_wine_ev.en: He finally turns, gives you one look, and then — unexpectedly — pours a second glass and pushes it to the edge of the table. "Standing's uncomfortable." It's as close to 'please sit' as he gets.

fushen_c1_b1_wine_he.en: He pours a second glass and pushes it to the edge of the table. "Standing's uncomfortable." That is the entire invitation and there will not be a warmer one. When you thank him he looks back out at the city. "It was going to waste. Don't read anything into it."

fushen_c1_b2_notice_ev.en: "You're not looking at this apartment, and you're not looking at me," he says suddenly, a flicker of real interest for the first time. "You're looking at that one streetlight that never goes off. Why?"

fushen_c1_b2_notice_he.en: "You're not looking at the apartment, and you're not looking at me." It is the first thing he has said with any interest in it. "You're watching the one streetlight on that corner that never goes off. Why." Not a question, in his mouth. It is still, unmistakably, a question.

fushen_c1_b3_name_ev.en: As you leave, he stops you, pauses, as if unused to asking such things. "Your name." — not phrased as a question, yet you can tell he genuinely wants to know.

fushen_c1_b3_name_he.en: "Your name." Not phrased as a request; he does not appear to know how. When you give it he doesn't repeat it and doesn't thank you. He simply files it somewhere permanent, and somehow you can tell that he has. "...Good night. The driver is downstairs. He'll take you."

fushen_c1_c1a_q.en: He watches you over his glass, tone unreadable. "Most people come through that door to get something from me. What do you want?"

fushen_c1_c1a_r0.en: He arches a brow and, unusually, doesn't order her out at once. "…Rare," he says.

fushen_c1_c1a_r1.en: He's silent two seconds, his gaze resting on her face a moment. "…You don't talk like someone who wandered in by mistake."

fushen_c1_c1a_r2.en: He glances at the glass, the corner of his mouth moving almost imperceptibly. "…You have a mouth on you."

fushen_c1_c1b_q.en: You're finally leaving. He says suddenly, "The elevator on this floor needs access." And he sets a black keycard on the table, not looking at you.

fushen_c1_c1b_r0.en: "Don't flatter yourself." He looks away. "…I simply can't be bothered to come down and let you in each time."

fushen_c1_c1b_r1.en: He holds your gaze a moment, then looks away first. "…Get home safely."

fushen_c1_c1b_r2.en: He draws the card back, expression cool. "Suit yourself." But you notice he doesn't actually put it away.

fushen_c2_open.en: A week later, filling in for a friend at a gala, you unexpectedly run into him again. Surrounded by the crowd, his face gives away nothing, like a mountain that permits only distant viewing. But when he sees you across the room, his step falters almost imperceptibly — and then he leaves the partner chattering at his side stranded, and walks straight toward you.

fushen_c2_b1_remember_ev.en: A waiter brings drinks. He raises a hand to wave off the champagne and asks for a glass of warm water for you instead — you mentioned once that you can't really drink. He says nothing about it.

fushen_c2_b1_remember_he.en: He waves the champagne tray off before it reaches you and asks for warm water instead — you said once, weeks ago, that you can't really drink. He doesn't mention it. When you notice he's already looking elsewhere. "The champagne here is mediocre," he says. "You'd have regretted it."

fushen_c2_b2_rumor_ev.en: Nearby, someone murmurs: 'They say this Fu heir is ice through and through — he acquired his own brother's company overnight.' He clearly hears it, but his face doesn't change; only his hand tightens on the glass for an instant.

fushen_c2_b2_rumor_he.en: The murmur carries — *acquired his own brother's company overnight.* His face does not move; only his hand tightens on the glass for a fraction. He offers nothing. If you ask him directly and gently, it comes in as few words as possible: "The creditors would have taken everything he had. It was faster my way. He doesn't know. Leave it."

fushen_c2_b3_leave_ev.en: A very important figure tries to pull him away to talk business. He glances at his watch, then at you, and tells the man flatly, "Another day." — for you, he brushes off the most important person at the gala.

fushen_c2_b3_leave_he.en: The most important man in the room wants ten minutes. Fu Shen glances at his watch, then at you. "Another day," he tells him, and turns back, as though it cost nothing. It cost something. He does not intend for you to be told what.

fushen_c2_c2a_q.en: Away from the crowd, he asks abruptly, "You heard what they said. Do you think that's the kind of man I am?"

fushen_c2_c2a_r0.en: He's silent a long while, eyes on the wine in his glass. "…You're the first to put it that way."

fushen_c2_c2a_r1.en: He turns to look at her, a crack running through the ice in his eyes. "…Then tell me. What is it you see."

fushen_c2_c2a_r2.en: For once he's caught off guard, and looks away. "…Some things, no one believes even when you explain."

fushen_c2_c2b_q.en: The gala ends; it's raining outside. His car waits at the door, the driver holding the rear passenger seat open. He stands at your side, not getting in.

fushen_c2_c2b_r0.en: He steps aside to let her in first, tone flat. "Get in. Don't get wet." — but he holds the umbrella almost entirely over her.

fushen_c2_c2b_r1.en: He looks at her, doesn't insist — but has the driver wait until her cab arrives before leaving.

fushen_c2_c2b_r2.en: He goes still. After a moment, he opens the door a little wider. "…Get in. Ride through this rain with me for a while."

fushen_c3_open.en: Out of nowhere, he invites you to the Fu family estate — a place even business partners can't enter. The car glides down a long tree-lined drive and stops before a century-old mansion. The butler and a row of staff are already waiting at the door. You've barely stepped out, no time to feel awkward, when the old butler bows deeply and says respectfully, "Young Madam. You've had a long journey. The master told us to expect you." You freeze — when did he ever introduce you to his household like that?

fushen_c3_b1_madam_ev.en: You turn to him, wanting to ask about 'Young Madam'. But his face doesn't change; he only straightens your collar, ruffled by the wind. "It's just what they're used to saying. Pay it no mind." — yet he neither denies it nor corrects them.

fushen_c3_b1_madam_he.en: You open your mouth to ask about *Young Madam* and he reaches over and straightens the collar the wind has turned up, eyes somewhere past your shoulder. "It's what they're used to saying. Pay it no mind." He does not correct one member of his staff, then or later.

fushen_c3_b2_room_ev.en: The butler leads you to a guest room, but you find it already arranged to your taste — the flowers you once mentioned liking, the books you read, even the warm color temperature of the bedside lamp. He remembered every one.

fushen_c3_b2_room_he.en: Your flowers. Your books. The bedside lamp at the exact warm temperature you once complained no hotel ever gets right. "The housekeeper handles the rooms," he says, which would be more convincing if the housekeeper had ever met you. "If anything is wrong with it, say so and it will be changed tonight."

fushen_c3_c3a_q.en: That night you find him in the study. You finally ask, "'Young Madam'… you told them to call me that, didn't you?" His back is to you; his shoulders tense for an instant.

fushen_c3_c3a_r0.en: He turns around, and the iceberg in his eyes fully splits. "…This house has been cold for thirty years. I wanted it to have someone worth calling 'Madam'."

fushen_c3_c3a_r1.en: He's silent a long while, then says quietly, "…Some titles, I didn't want anyone to think were temporary."

fushen_c3_c3a_r2.en: His hand tightens on the glass. Very quietly: "…I've never brought anyone into this house. You tell me."

fushen_c3_c3b_q.en: The long corridor is cold. Noticing you shrink your shoulders, he takes off his coat and, without a word, drapes it over you, then keeps walking as if nothing happened.

fushen_c3_c3b_r0.en: "I'm not cold." He doesn't look back — but you notice he quietly slows, and falls into step beside you.

fushen_c3_c3b_r1.en: He says nothing, only matches his pace to yours. The lamp at the corridor's end — he'd had it lit in advance.

fushen_c3_c3b_r2.en: His step catches; he turns his face away. "…Don't talk nonsense. Keep it on, don't catch a chill." But a little warmth leaks at the edge of his ear.

fushen_c4_open.en: The Fu elders have arranged a family dinner — ostensibly to meet you, in truth an ambush. At the head sits the patriarch who rules the family. Over the meal, the elders mention lightly: another old family long ago arranged a marriage match for Fu Shen, and you are merely 'someone he brought in from outside'. A cheque is slid in front of you — leave, and the number is negotiable. Beside you, Fu Shen's face darkens.

fushen_c4_b1_cheque_ev.en: The cheque sits by your hand. Before Fu Shen can speak, you feel the pressure dropping off him in waves — but he waits, waits for you to react first, because he won't decide your dignity for you.

fushen_c4_b1_cheque_he.en: The cheque slides to rest by your hand. Fu Shen does not speak. The air around him has gone very cold and very still, and still he waits — he will not price you in front of you, or answer for you. Only when you have met it does he turn to his family, quietly: "Now. My turn."

fushen_c4_b2_stand_ev.en: Fu Shen suddenly stands and, in front of every elder, pushes the arranged-marriage card back before the patriarch — the first time he has ever openly defied the entire family. "This match, I refuse," he says, not loudly, but it silences the whole hall.

fushen_c4_b2_stand_he.en: He stands and pushes the card back across the table to the patriarch. "This match, I refuse." Not loud. The hall goes silent anyway, because nobody in it has ever heard him refuse anything out loud. He moves one step sideways, between you and every elder in the room, and stays there.

fushen_c4_bx_after_hours_ev.en: The estate empties. The elders go, the staff are dismissed for the night, and for the first time in its hundred years the house has two people in it and nobody else.

fushen_c4_bx_after_hours_he.en: "I have refused them for you," he says, "and that obliges you to nothing. I want that understood before anything else is." He is standing very straight, which is what he does instead of trembling. "I would like you to stay tonight. If the answer is no it will not cost you one thing — not the room, not the house, not me." The answer is not no. Something in his shoulders finally lets go, and he crosses the distance he has been refusing to cross since the first glass of wine, and after that the old house keeps its own counsel.

fushen_c4_c4a_q.en: The patriarch fixes his eyes on you and says slowly, "Name your price. The Fu family can afford it." Fu Shen moves to answer for you — you press his hand down. This one, you want to answer yourself.

fushen_c4_c4a_r0.en: Silence in the hall. Under the table, Fu Shen quietly turns his hand to grip yours, fingers tightening — a silent thank-you he's never given before.

fushen_c4_c4a_r1.en: The patriarch's expression shifts. Fu Shen looks at her, and for the first time something close to pride surfaces in his eyes. "She's right."

fushen_c4_c4a_r2.en: Fu Shen finally speaks, voice cold. "I obeyed this family once. This time, I listen to her."

fushen_c4_c4a_r3.en: He does not move a step closer. He does not go back either. "Very well," he says. "I will stay here."

fushen_c4_c4b_q.en: The dinner breaks up badly. Back in the study, he stands at the window with his back to you, shoulders rigid. "…I let you be humiliated tonight. I never should have brought you into this family."

fushen_c4_c4b_r0.en: He goes stiff, then slowly covers your hands with his, voice low. "…This house has been cold for thirty years. Tonight, for the first time, it felt warm."

fushen_c4_c4b_r1.en: He turns to face her, an emotion he never shows churning in his eyes. "…I thought I'd never do such a thing for anyone in my life."

fushen_c4_c4b_r2.en: He finally turns, slowly reaches out, and pulls you into his arms — the first time in his life he has held someone of his own will.

fushen_c5_open.en: The family storm has passed. He didn't compromise, and he wasn't cast out — in his usual way, coldly and completely, he settled everything that needed settling. This morning, for the first time, no staff hover on the terrace. He pours you a cup of coffee himself — the way you take it: a touch of sugar, a hint of cinnamon. As he hands it over, his fingertips pause for a moment. "First time in my life I've poured coffee for anyone," he says lightly — but you know the weight of it.

fushen_c5_b1_offer_ev.en: "The family wants me to take over the entire overseas division. London. Five years at least." He looks toward the city, then pauses. "I haven't given them an answer."

fushen_c5_b1_offer_he.en: "The family wants me to take the overseas division. London. Five years, at least." He watches the skyline go pale. "I haven't given them an answer." He does not say that yours decides his. He simply stops talking, and waits, and gives away nothing at all.

fushen_c5_b2_truth_ev.en: He finally turns to look at you and says something he has never said to anyone in his life: "Nothing I've ever owned was something I actually wanted to keep. Until you."

fushen_c5_b2_truth_he.en: He turns and looks at you. "Nothing I have ever owned was something I actually wanted to keep." A pause with nothing in it — no joke coming, no retreat. "Until you." Then he says nothing more and lets it stand there in the open between you, which for him is an act of enormous violence.

fushen_c5_bx_morning_ev.en: Dawn on the terrace. No staff. A pot of coffee he made himself, badly.

fushen_c5_bx_morning_he.en: "I have never eaten breakfast in this house without an audience," he says, and drinks the bad coffee anyway. Then, without any particular ceremony, he moves his chair around to your side of the table. "This is better. We will do it this way from now on."

fushen_c5_c5a_q.en: "So what do you want now?" — you're the one asking. He looks at you for a long moment, then slowly holds out his hand.

fushen_c5_c5a_r0.en: He grips your hand, his voice softer than you've ever heard. "I'm not going to London. This house has been cold thirty years — I want to warm it, with you."

fushen_c5_c5a_r1.en: He lowers his eyes, rarely, and when he lifts them there's no ice left at all. "I want you. This one thing, I won't weigh, and I won't explain."

fushen_c5_c5a_r2.en: His hand stops in mid-air, and it's a long while before he draws it back. "…You're right." He looks away, and the iceberg slowly closes over again.

fushen_c5_c5a_r3.en: "...That is the correct order," he says, after a moment. "I had them the wrong way round. Thank you."

guyan_end_he_forever_2.en: A year later, a small line appeared beneath the sign: "Umbrellas lent free on rainy days — please return them. Or come back another day and share a pot of tea."

guyan_end_he_forever_3.en: Every rainy evening someone pushes the door open to escape the rain, and the chime rings softly. You look up from behind the counter; he looks up from the stacks; and you smile at each other.

guyan_end_he_forever_4.en: The book of poems still sits in the most visible spot. There are three lines on the flyleaf now — the third one is yours: "I came. And I'm not leaving."

guyan_end_he_forever_5.en: Dango rolls over lazily, claiming the patch of light that belongs to the two of you. The shop keeps its own hours now, and so do the two of you.

guyan_end_he_slow_t.en: The Kind of Love That Takes Its Time

guyan_end_he_slow_1.en: He never said the whole sentence, and you never rushed him.

guyan_end_he_slow_2.en: Some kinds of love are like old books — you turn them one page at a time.

guyan_end_he_slow_3.en: Now you come every week: sorting books, feeding the cat, reading whole afternoons by the window. Neither of you has ever said it outright, but on the days you're due, he brews an extra pot of osmanthus oolong; and on the evenings he's swamped, you flip the 'Open' sign for him.

guyan_end_he_slow_4.en: "No rush," he says one day, looking at you, his ears still going pink. "I waited years for this shop. For you — I'm happy to take my time."

guyan_end_he_slow_5.en: Outside, it starts to rain again. This time, you both have umbrellas. The shop keeps its own hours now, and so do the two of you.

guyan_end_be_missed_t.en: Only a Line Between the Pages

guyan_end_be_missed_1.en: Later you moved to another city.

guyan_end_be_missed_2.en: Before leaving, you visited the shop one last time. He was still there, and Dango, and that warm amber lamp. You put the book of poems back on the shelf and didn't take it with you.

guyan_end_be_missed_3.en: "Travel safe," he said at the door, smiling softly — the same way he had the night he lent you the umbrella.

guyan_end_be_missed_4.en: Years on, you still think of that shop sometimes, and the faded line on the flyleaf.

guyan_end_be_missed_5.en: Some words, the moment they're written, already know they may not be for the one who stays. You just happened, once, to read them. The shop keeps its own hours now, and so do the two of you.

ethan_end_he_stay_t.en: The Light Stays On For You

ethan_end_he_stay_2.en: Three months later the top floor became a public library — open at night, for people who work the night shift. On opening day, a brass plaque bore a security guard's name.

ethan_end_he_stay_3.en: Standing beside you, he said, "My father would have liked this."

ethan_end_he_stay_4.en: Then he looked down at you. "I didn't buy this one. We built it." The top-floor light stays off. Two adults, one city, and no meeting behind it.

ethan_end_he_together_2.en: But on the third weekend of every month, the light on that top floor comes on — he flies back, cancels everything, for one drink and one conversation.

ethan_end_he_together_3.en: In the seventh month he sent a photo late at night: the glow of another city outside another window.

ethan_end_he_together_4.en: The caption was four words. "Still not the same." The top-floor light stays off. Two adults, one city, and no meeting behind it.

ethan_end_be_distance_t.en: Just a Light on a Top Floor

ethan_end_be_distance_2.en: You still pass that building sometimes. The top floor is lit some nights, dark on others.

ethan_end_be_distance_4.en: Some people are just a floor in your life — you pressed the wrong button once, and then the right one back. The top-floor light stays off. Two adults, one city, and no meeting behind it.

luxingye_end_he_forever_t.en: From Row Seven to the Stage

luxingye_end_he_forever_1.en: Two years later, his independent studio held its first arena show.

luxingye_end_he_forever_2.en: Again, on the last encore, he suddenly stopped the band. The arena went silent; tens of thousands held their breath — every longtime fan knew what was coming.

luxingye_end_he_forever_3.en: But this time, he didn't look toward row seven.

luxingye_end_he_forever_4.en: He turned around and reached a hand toward the back of the stage — and you walked out from the wings and took it.

luxingye_end_he_forever_5.en: "I used to confess to the person in row seven," he told the whole arena, smiling, but his eyes only on you. "Now, I've invited her up on stage."

luxingye_end_he_forever_6.en: A galaxy of light rose for the two of you. As the intro to 'Row Seven' began, you finally understood: some people take two whole years to walk from the seats to the stage — and every step is worth it. No call time, no cameras, no one waiting for either of you to be someone else.

luxingye_end_he_quiet_t.en: The Show With an Audience of One

luxingye_end_he_quiet_1.en: He never returned to the arena stage, and he never missed it.

luxingye_end_he_quiet_2.en: That tiny livehouse became his home turf. Fewer fans — but every one of them truly understood him.

luxingye_end_he_quiet_3.en: You never made a grand public announcement, and never hid, either. At the end of every show he'd play a song he never named, then look toward one fixed spot in the crowd — row seven, always kept for you.

luxingye_end_he_quiet_4.en: "Know which show is my favorite?" he asked one night after closing.

luxingye_end_he_quiet_6.en: He slung the guitar onto his back, leaned in, and grinned. "The ones I play just for you at home. Zero bad reviews." No call time, no cameras, no one waiting for either of you to be someone else.

luxingye_end_be_lights_out_1.en: The confession was quietly buried by the label; the official statement called it an improvised stage moment.

luxingye_end_be_lights_out_2.en: You never appeared on any camera, and you never went back to row seven.

luxingye_end_be_lights_out_3.en: He's still the top idol adored by millions, his smile still flawless. Only sometimes, on an encore, he looks toward one direction in the crowd, pauses for half a second, then carries on as if nothing happened.

luxingye_end_be_lights_out_4.en: Years later you still keep that row-seven ticket stub.

luxingye_end_be_lights_out_5.en: You once heard a song in its raw form — backstage at midnight, no lights, no makeup, just a convenience-store rice ball. That version, no one in the world heard but you. And that's enough. No call time, no cameras, no one waiting for either of you to be someone else.

liam_end_he_home_1.en: A year later, the fence that once divided the two yards came down.

liam_end_he_home_2.en: Between the two houses there was now one shared backyard. String lights covered the new porch, and his mother's chili was always simmering on the grill. Biscuit got his own dog door and wandered between yards as he pleased — it was all home now, either way.

liam_end_he_home_3.en: He's still a firefighter, still scared every single time. But now, before every call-out, he glances back at the singed leather cord you tied to his mirror.

liam_end_he_home_4.en: "Just a keepsake," he always says. "Reminds me there's a home I've got to make it back to."

liam_end_he_home_5.en: Your grandmother's watch sits on the porch windowsill now. She used to say: hold on to the people who show up.

liam_end_he_home_6.en: He showed up. And every single time, he comes home safe. Two chairs, one porch, and nobody's shift starting in the morning.

liam_end_he_slow_t.en: The Neighbor Who Took His Time

liam_end_he_slow_1.en: You didn't rush into the same house.

liam_end_he_slow_2.en: Some good things are worth taking slow.

liam_end_he_slow_3.en: He took the position and fought to base the unit near you. You still kept your own yards — only the gate in that fence was never locked again. Coming off a night shift, he'd swing by your side first, check your faucet for drips, and mooch a breakfast while he was at it.

liam_end_he_slow_4.en: "I'm not in a hurry," he grinned over the fence one morning, Biscuit crowding his feet. "got the girl next door, got the dog, got a sink to fix now and then. Man's gotta pace himself."

liam_end_he_slow_5.en: Your grandmother's watch is still on your wrist, keeping perfect time.

liam_end_he_slow_6.en: Some people don't need grand gestures. He's just there — every single day. Two chairs, one porch, and nobody's shift starting in the morning.

liam_end_be_moved_t.en: The Door Next Door That Never Knocked Again

liam_end_be_moved_1.en: He took the position and moved three states away.

liam_end_be_moved_2.en: Before he left, he polished your grandmother's watch spotless, handed it back with care, and smiled that same warm smile. "You take care of yourself, alright? And that sink — call a plumber, don't let it drip."

liam_end_be_moved_3.en: New neighbors moved in next door. No more golden retriever wagging in the yard, no more familiar whistle at dusk.

liam_end_be_moved_4.en: Sometimes you think of the man who always grinned and said 'it's my whole job', and of the night he ran into the firelight and walked out safe.

liam_end_be_moved_5.en: Some people are like a fire passing through — so warm, so bright, you think you can stay close forever. But in the end, he has to run to the next place that needs him.

liam_end_be_moved_6.en: Your grandmother said, hold on to the people who show up.

liam_end_be_moved_7.en: You couldn't hold on. But you remember — he really did show up. Two chairs, one porch, and nobody's shift starting in the morning.

adrian_end_he_forever_1.en: A year later, he never went back to any label.

adrian_end_he_forever_2.en: He started his own tiny imprint and releases only what he wants. No viral collabs, no rewrites. It's not the biggest-selling thing — but every song is real.

adrian_end_he_forever_3.en: The song that was almost sold off finally came out complete, not one word changed. Its title was a single letter: 'U.'

adrian_end_he_forever_4.en: In the liner notes, under songwriters, there was his name — and one other.

adrian_end_he_forever_5.en: "People keep asking who the song's about," he said one late night, curled in the little home studio that's yours now, guitar in his arms, smiling with no defenses left. "I finally tell them the truth these days."

adrian_end_he_forever_7.en: He struck a chord, leaned in close, his voice that smoke-grey 3 a.m. tenderness. "…that I never wrote a single one that wasn't." The song is finished, the case stays shut, and neither of you is hiding anything.

adrian_end_he_quiet_1.en: He never climbed back to the top, and he didn't care.

adrian_end_he_quiet_2.en: That underground livehouse became his regular haunt. Small crowds — but every one of them truly understood him.

adrian_end_he_quiet_3.en: You never made any grand public thing of it. He's still all swagger on stage and silence off it — except with you. He still writes what he means into songs, only he's stopped flatly denying every word; and each time he finishes one, he plays it for you first, watching your face, more nervous than he ever was before an arena.

adrian_end_he_quiet_4.en: "Know the difference between the songs I release and the ones I don't?" he asked one night after closing.

adrian_end_he_quiet_6.en: He slung the guitar onto his back, leaned in, and smiled slow and dangerous. "…the ones I don't release, I only ever play for you. And those are the good ones." The song is finished, the case stays shut, and neither of you is hiding anything.

adrian_end_be_unreleased_1.en: In the end, he never released the song, and never changed it.

adrian_end_be_unreleased_2.en: He locked it away with the demos that will never see daylight, alongside every other thing he refused to admit he felt.

adrian_end_be_unreleased_3.en: You two fell out of touch. He's still the untamed rockstar on stage, singing the catchy songs that sell so well, a distance in his smile that no one can cross.

adrian_end_be_unreleased_4.en: Only sometimes, near the end of a show when all the lights go down, he'll suddenly stop and play, alone, a melody no one has heard — just a few bars — then slide back into the next song as if nothing happened.

adrian_end_be_unreleased_5.en: No one knows what it is.

adrian_end_be_unreleased_6.en: Only you do — a song never finished, never sung all the way through for anyone. It came, once, so close to being yours. The song is finished, the case stays shut, and neither of you is hiding anything.

fushen_end_he_warm_house_t.en: The House That Was Cold for Thirty Years

fushen_end_he_warm_house_2.en: A year later, the century-old Fu estate was hung with red for the first time. The butler and staff stood in two rows — but this time, you weren't a guest being introduced. You were the mistress of the house.

fushen_end_he_warm_house_3.en: Many of the old rules changed. The cold crystal chandeliers gave way to warm light; the flowers you love appeared on the terrace; and in the study, beside his shelves, stood a whole new row of your books.

fushen_end_he_warm_house_4.en: That morning, again, you drank coffee he'd poured himself — a touch of sugar, a hint of cinnamon.

fushen_end_he_warm_house_5.en: "I used to think everything I owned in this life was bought," he said, wrapping his arms around you from behind, chin resting on your hair, voice low. "You're the only thing I ever asked for."

fushen_end_he_warm_house_6.en: Downstairs, the butler told the newest servant with a smile: "When the Young Madam is here, the master's face is… far easier to look at than it used to be." The old house has learned to be quiet for two people instead of none.

fushen_end_he_slow_thaw_t.en: A Man Who Thaws an Inch at a Time

fushen_end_he_slow_thaw_1.en: He's still the man who's cold to the whole world.

fushen_end_he_slow_thaw_3.en: You never held any grand ceremony — he dislikes noise, and you understand him. But the Fu household gradually learned: the master who never let anyone stay the night now leaves the study lamp burning until you're home; the coffee he never poured for anyone now waits, a cup for you, every morning.

fushen_end_he_slow_thaw_4.en: He still rarely says things like 'I need you'.

fushen_end_he_slow_thaw_5.en: But once, when you came back late from a trip and pushed open the door, you saw that in the whole cold estate, only the lamp in the entryway was lit — for you.

fushen_end_he_slow_thaw_6.en: And you knew. Some people never have to say it. He tucked 'I need you', an inch at a time, into every detail he kept lit for you. The old house has learned to be quiet for two people instead of none.

fushen_end_be_glass_2.en: Before leaving, he left you the black keycard and said, "This floor. You can come up any time." But you both knew — some access opens elevators, not hearts.

fushen_end_be_glass_3.en: You still pass that penthouse tower sometimes. The floor-to-ceiling windows on the top floor are lit some nights, dark on others.

fushen_end_be_glass_4.en: You never used the card again.

fushen_end_be_glass_5.en: Some people are like a city skyline seen through glass — beautiful, close, near enough to count every light. And yet, always, one pane of glass away.

fushen_end_be_glass_6.en: He never explained himself. And so, in the end, you never quite made it inside. The old house has learned to be quiet for two people instead of none.
